samples.summary: Read-only Copy is still unreachable inside a table: the table menu bails on readOnly and the body menu bails on isInTable(), so the change's new read-only Copy never appears for in-table right-clicks
samples.evidence: `docs-table-context-menu.tsx:70` returns early when `readOnly`, with the comment (line 69) claiming "the (edit-free) body context menu handles the right-click". But `docs-context-menu.tsx:68` returns early when `editor.isInTable()`. So in read-only mode a right-click with a selection inside a table cell opens no menu at all, and the newly enabled `showCopy = hasSelection` (docs-context-menu.tsx:181) does not apply there. Either the body menu needs to stop bailing on `isInTable()` in read-only, or the table menu needs a Copy-only read-only branch; the comment at docs-table-context-menu.tsx:69 is also now inaccurate.

samples.summary: Third copy of the platform-detection regex: the new modifier check in editor.ts duplicates TextEditor's own isMac derivation, so the two can drift
samples.evidence: The new `imageKeyHandler` computes `const mod = /Mac|iPhone|iPad|iPod/.test(navigator.platform) ? e.metaKey : e.ctrlKey` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2295-2297), duplicating `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:874-875` (`const isMac = /Mac|iPhone|iPad|iPod/.test(navigator.platform); const mod = isMac ? metaKey : ctrlKey;`). The whole point of the new branch is to agree exactly with `handleKeyDown`'s notion of the copy/cut chord; because the detection is copied rather than shared, a future change to the mac test (e.g. moving to `navigator.userAgentData.platform`, which `shortcuts-catalog.ts` already takes as a parameter) will fix one site and silently reintroduce the #870 clearing behaviour at the other. Fix belongs on the new code: extract/reuse one helper.
